title: Sequoia’s Roelof Botha: 60% of Our Capital Went into AI Over the Past 12 Months
summary: Emily: Sequoia’s market memos are famous — 2008’s “R.I.P. Good Times,” more recently “adapt” and “endure.” What’s the signal now?
author: Unique Research
html:
Unique Research · Insight · October 24, 2023 · Interview with Sequoia Capital steward Roelof Botha (host Emily)

Core takeaways

  • Fundamentals first: build the business and serve customers — the only things founders control. Some companies should revisit product–market fit to unlock more potential.
  • Macro: the easy-money era is ending, but great companies were built in high-rate and recession environments alike (Apple, Cisco, PayPal as Sequoia examples).
  • Sequoia’s horizon: long-term company potential over short-term stock marks; selective post-IPO hold via the Horizon / “durable capital” structure.
  • Europe: ~1/3 of global software talent; more founders spinning out of platforms with ambition to build globally; Sequoia optimistic; met UK PM Sunak.
  • AI: Sequoia is a large AI investor — 60% of capital deployed in the past 12 months around AI; many still “stealth”; potential compared to internet, cloud, and mobile.
  • Beyond AI: bioinformatics, personalized medicine, defense tech; conviction on X (ex-Twitter).
  • Where to start: Silicon Valley still #1 for funding concentration (~50% of VC), but talent is distributed — build anywhere.

Market message: “focus on fundamentals”

Emily: Sequoia’s market memos are famous — 2008’s “R.I.P. Good Times,” more recently “adapt” and “endure.” What’s the signal now?

Botha: Focus on fundamentals. At PayPal in early 2000, after the crash, they had about seven months of runway and zero revenue. The only controllable lever was building a business that served customers. That is still Sequoia’s advice. A twist: some portfolio companies have incomplete PMF or untapped potential — they should go back to first principles and ask if a different path unlocks a higher ceiling.

Macro and the racing-line metaphor

Jamie Dimon’s 7% rate worry: Botha agrees easy money is over. Sequoia’s 50+ year history: Apple (1978) when 10-year yields were >8%; Cisco (1987) similar; PayPal and Google (1999) above 6%. Today’s 10-year around ~4.5%. Great companies get built in all rate regimes.

On the racing metaphor: approach the apex, then accelerate out. Botha thinks they are near the apex — leading companies are pressing the advantage and flooring it.

Instacart, post-IPO hold, and “stewardship”

Sequoia invested in 2013 at a ~$29M valuation when the team was <10 people. Pre-pandemic 2019 revenue ~$214M; last year ~$2.5B; H1 free cash flow already exceeded all of 2019 revenue. The 2021 late-stage mark (~$39B then, ~$8B around IPO talk) was underwater — but four other financings were highly profitable. Only two prices matter: entry and exit. Public marks bounce daily; Sequoia underwrites the long company.

On criticism (e.g. Fred Wilson) of holding post-IPO: Sequoia’s Horizon / durable capital structure put ~95–96% of available capital into vehicles that can hold longer. MongoDB IPO’d near what would be ~$23/share in today’s terms and later traded near $350 — >90% of value created after listing. Google went from ~$23B IPO market cap toward ~$1T+; Nvidia was a Sequoia seed in 1993 at ~$300M IPO and is now a trillion-dollar company. Hold selectively where long conviction exists.

Botha on being called “steward”: Sequoia was named for trees that live 2,000+ years — leave the partnership better than you found it; recruit so juniors inherit the firm, not just work for you.

Europe, China separation, AI allocation

Europe: one team, one fund searching Western market leaders — Romania or Copenhagen alike. ~1/3 of software developers live in Europe; platform spinouts (e.g. from Revolut’s ecosystem) plus rising founder ambition. High-level EU regulation, Botha argues, doesn’t really change seed founding or young founders’ global ambition — like rates don’t stop good ideas.

On formal separation from China/India franchises: independent businesses by region; more cousin-style collaboration than sibling rivalry.

AI: “We’ve been very active at seed. Over the past 12 months, 60% of our investments have been around AI.” 1990s internet boom → trough of disillusionment ~2002 → internet mattered more than anyone imagined. AI may rhyme. Compared to internet, cloud, mobile. Possibly a record number of stealth AI bets — five deals this year where Sequoia found the team and agreed terms before the company even incorporated.

Beyond AI: healthcare, bioinformatics, personalized medicine, defense tech. On X: Elon gave Botha his first U.S. job offer 23 years ago at x.com; Sequoia is “passionate” about cost structure, faster product cycles, record usage, business-model reset, and transparent moderation — early days (<12 months since acquisition vs Sequoia’s usual 10–15 year hold).

Best place to found today: Silicon Valley still ~50% of VC dollars last 12 months, then NY/LA, then London, Paris close. What matters most is assembling talent — PMs, designers, finance people who understand tech companies — not capital alone. Sequoia wants great founders everywhere.

Next era label: after move-fast / year-of-efficiency — back to fundamentals: serve customers, clear line of sight, build a great business model.
